content: 1. The use of certain medications is contraindicated due to the potential for severe hypotension or syncope. Close monitoring is required in such cases. 2. Fluconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of darunavir via the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of inhaled flunisolide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Darunavir also increases fluoxetine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor antidepressant response and adjust doses as needed. 6. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. Cobicistat also increases flurazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of flutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect on flutamide. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases fluticasone furoate levels. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate systemic corticosteroid exposure, leading to adverse effects such as Cushing syndrome. Monitor closely for signs of corticosteroid toxicity. 9. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may exacerbate systemic corticosteroid adverse effects. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with darunavir, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 11. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of cobicistat through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust antidepressant doses to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose. 12. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Fosaprepitant also increases darunavir levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 15. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat is similarly affected by fosphenytoin. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 16. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406, the active metabolite of fostamatinib. Monitor for toxicities and adjust the fostamatinib dose as needed. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase futibatinib toxicities. 18. Garlic decreases darunavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of gefitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Cobicistat has a similar effect on gefitinib. 20. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. 22. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with darunavir, a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 24. Darunavir decreases the effects of glimepiride through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. 25. Darunavir may increase or decrease glipizide levels. Use alternatives if available. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 26. Darunavir decreases the effects of glyburide through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 27. Grapefruit increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Green tea may increase the risk of bleeding when combined with darunavir. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Griseofulvin decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. Reduce the guanfacine dose to half the recommended amount if co-administered. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may result in potentially fatal respiratory depression. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hydrocortisone decreases darunavir levels via the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If short-term use is necessary, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 36. Idelalisib increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and adjust doses as needed. 37. Cobicistat decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Use alternatives if available. Monitor closely for toxicity. 38. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a minor effect on imatinib levels. Monitor closely. 40. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust antidepressant doses to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose. Monitor closely during co-administration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use is contraindicated due to the risk of hyperbilirubinemia.
